trials.root_cause: The indexed exact-ID fix #101 enabled real model-controlled creation of an editable empty Velorn project. After successful create_project, the controller invalidated project presence to 'unknown' rather than independently re-reading get_project. The 2B model then searched broad terms, repeatedly retried create_project on an already existing project, and stopped on a reported native write error. This run proves neither media editing nor export.
trials.next_safety_fix: Use one trusted post-write get_project READ after a model-chosen project_open enabling operation, record immutable read evidence and preserve actual project identity in the next inference context. Still requires independent live model end-to-end trial.
trials.source_proof_scope: Runner-uploaded ZIP SHA independently checked in artifact reader; project.comfystudio contained one empty timeline and no assets. Human creative acceptance not attempted.

trials.root_cause: The stronger 4B independently selected create_project but used its default previewOnly=true, receiving a host response with success=false, result.previewOnly=true and no applied project. A second model-selected create_project with previewOnly=false created an empty native project. The controller nonetheless counted the preview plan as a successful native write. Project presence was then set to unknown; the model repeatedly invoked create_project and terminated on a native reported write error without timeline edits/exports.
trials.next_safety_fix: Distinguish preview-only host responses from acknowledged applied writes, independently read actual native project presence after create/open when granted read-only access, and preserve proof that 2B/4B failed real creative acceptance. Do not claim performance superiority from these different incomplete runs.

trials.failure: After a model-selected project preview and real create_project, the native project remained empty (0 imported assets, 0 clips). The host-observed import_asset_from_path capability was visible, but the 2B model selected timeline markers. Its first native marker write was acknowledged and persisted three markers. On turn nine it submitted add_timeline_markers with previewOnly:true. At the exact pinned Velorn commit b3c02adbd5c0779feb8abf34978299e9502cc0e7, electron/mcpServer.js addTimelineMarkers intercepts previewOnly:true BEFORE the mutating renderer action and returns a top-level {previewOnly:true,markerCount,markers} receipt WITHOUT a success/action/result wrapper. The ZX7 controller only accepted legacy nested preview shapes and wrongly classified this safe native preview as unconfirmed write, terminating the model session. The downstream renderer handler (mcpActions.js) ignores previewOnly because the actual Electron MCP entrypoint filters it first; examining the renderer in isolation led to a prior incorrect diagnosis. Source imports, active clips, media export and real frame observations all remained zero. Stored project demonstrates three earlier applied markers, not a completed creative edit.
trials.next_falsification: Correct ZX7 native controller to parse exactly source-verified Electron MCP top-level marker previews only when the model actually requests previewOnly:true; preserve anti-replay and unexpected response fail-closed semantics. Remove the erroneous shared-client preview blockade. Verify corrected code with adversarial source-shaped unit tests and physical 2B/4B model+native editor evaluation; no artistic acceptance claimed.

trials.failure: The first Qwen3.5-4B/native run to pass source import and actual timeline placement. Real model created project, imported an original synthetic H.264 video into Velorn, model-previewed add_assets_to_timeline without mutation and then explicitly committed the batch placement. The saved editable .comfystudio contained one enabled four-second video clip referencing a real project asset on visible unlocked Video Feed track. The seventh model decision exceeded the existing 300s per-request limit: model-server logs independently show 5,678 prompt tokens processed in 258.51s, then response generation started but was aborted at 300s. Model could not proceed to an actual export, physical frame observation, or independent revision. CPU-only free-runner latency, repeated prompt reprocessing and poor KV-prefix continuity are now the primary measured bottleneck, not failure to import or place native video.
trials.next_falsification: Reorder otherwise identical host-current local prompt fields to preserve a reusable static prefix for llama.cpp; do not remove schemas, editorial evidence or model-selected actions. Reevaluate end-to-end with a faster stronger preexisting NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B agent under synthetic-only cloud consent; the original CPU 4B would need a significantly larger time budget to finish 48 decisions.
